 GREEN AND WILLIAMSON CRANES COUNTIES                           §



 POST HEARING REPLY BRIEF, PROPOSED FINDINGS OF FACT, CONCLUSIONS
                OF LAW AND ORDERING PROVISIONS​
                 OF INTERVENOR GEORGE NOELKE

COMES NOW, George Noelke (“Noelke”), pro se, to submit his Post Hearing Reply Brief with
Proposed Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law and Ordering Provisions, pursuant to SOAH Order Nos. 6
and 32 in this case.

  I.​   Introduction
    A.​ Intervenor George Noelke ("Noelke") submits this Reply Brief to address the fundamental
        evidentiary and legal deficiencies in the Applicant’s case.
    B.​ Noelke has previously filed his post hearing brief in 59182 that made certain recommendations
        for Proposed Findings of Face (FOF), Conclusions of Law (COL) and ordering provisions. See
        Item 544 in 59182. None of his recommendations were adopted by the ALJ. See PFD at 537.
        Noelke has also filed exceptions to the PFD in 59182. Item 544. His recommendations in 59182
        are relevant to this case because all proposed routes in 59475 will cross or parallel the Eiger and
        Matterhorn pipelines.
 II.​   Reservation of rights to file Exceptions to the PFD in 59475 for en masse dismissal
   A.​ Noelke files this formal reservation of rights to protect the administrative and appellate record
       regarding the unconstitutional en masse disposal, default, or constructive exclusion of the 839 pro
       se Intervenors in this docket.
   1.​ The record establishes a systemic, structural defect compounded by the Applicants' and the ALJs’
       notice failures and the compressed timelines of SOAH Procedural Order No. 6. Specifically,
       numerous Texas citizens who filed timely motions to intervene on the last day of the deadline
       were not formally recognized or processed as Intervenors until after the deadlines to submit
       pre-filed direct testimony or written Statements of Position under 16 TAC § 22.124 had already
       lapsed.
   2.​ To execute a default or dismissal against pro se citizens for failing to comply with a deadline that
       expired before they were legally recognized as parties to the case is a procedural impossibility. It
       violates the core tenets of due course of law and due process provisions of the Texas and U.S.
       Constitutions. Texas Constitution, Tex. Const. art. I, § 19, the U.S. Constitution, U.S. Const.
       Amend XIV, § 1. This also violates the Texas equal protection clause. Texas Const. art 1, § 3
       Moreover, the Texas APA at Texas Gov’t Code § 2001.051(2) provides that Noelke, an Intervenor
       and thereby a “party” to this contested case, is “entitled to an opportunity…to respond and to
       present evidence and argument on each issue involved in the case.” Emphasis added. The en
       masse dismissal strips both Noelke and the dismissed Intervenors of their rights to fully litigate
       this case, thereby limiting their issues on appeal to the PUC Commissioners or to a Travis
       County District Court under the Texas APA at § 2001.174. See Item 5105 for Noelke’s expanded
       legal argument on these issues.
   3.​ A state actor cannot create a procedural trapdoor where compliance is legally impossible, and
       then leverage that impossibility to strip citizens of their property rights.
   4.​ Because the Applicants have now abandoned their "best meets" routing preference and requested
       that the Administrative Law Judges select any alternative route from the open map, the justiciable
       property interests of these 839 excluded citizens, especially those who filed to intervene on the
       last day of the deadline, remain actively exposed to a state-sanctioned taking without an
       opportunity to be heard.
   5.​ Applicants’ Initial Post Hearing Brief states that over 1,600 individuals and entities requested to
       intervene in this case. See Applicant’s Br. at p. 7, Item 6311. Of those, over 700 filed direct
       testimony or a statement of position and over 800 did not file direct testimony or a statement of
       position. Id. Applicants brief fails to disclose Noelke’s pleadings in protest of those dismissals.




                                                                                                              2
     6.​ Consequently, Intervenor Noelke explicitly reserves the right to raise these structural,
        notice-based, and constitutional defects via Special Exceptions to the Proposal for Decision
        pursuant to 16 TAC § 22.261(d), ensuring that this fatal jurisdictional and procedural error is fully
        preserved for Commission review and subsequent judicial review under Tex. Gov't Code §
        2001.174.

III. Matterhorn and Eiger Pipeline issues for the PFD in 59475

    A.​ Noelke’s evidence confirms that all proposed routes in 59475 cross or parallel the Matterhorn
        Express Pipeline. This means that multiple routes will cross the Eiger Express Pipeline at the
        same location. Noelke, Direct Testimony, Exh. 1, in 59182. This also means that Applicants’
        proposed line will cross 6.2 billion cubic feet of compressed natural gas daily at multiple
        locations in the 59182 and 59475 cases. Id.
    B.​ Applicants at the Hearing on the Merits of 59475 and in their Initial Brief presented no evidence
        or argument rebutting Noelke’s engineering constraint and AC mitigation costs issues raised by
        him regarding the Matterhorn and Eiger. No pipeline owners were intervenors in 59475.

VI. Conclusion​
Noelke requests FOF, COL and ordering provisions that reflect that Applicants have not proven that they
qualify for the CCN’s. Specifically, they have not by a preponderance of the evidence overcome the
engineering constraints presented by the Matterhorn and Eiger pipelines, nor have they addressed the
related costs of AC mitigation. Moreover, the PFD should reflect that Applicants improperly gained a
procedural advantage when they, without any substantive legal burden, obtained the dismissal of 839
intervenors en masse. Finally, Noelke has two ordering provisions he requests be included in the PFD.
First, the 839 intervenors should be reinstated as parties. And, second, in the alternative if a CCN is
approved he requests that he be recognized as having a lawful right to participate in AC mitigation
alongside the Applicants and the owners and operators of the pipelines.

WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Intervenor George Noelke respectfully prays that the
Honorable Administrative Law Judges not issue the CCN in 59475 and that they include the FOF, COL
and ordering provisions above requested by Noelke.

Signed June 26, 2026




                                                                                                            3
 Respectfully submitted,​
​
​
/s/ George Noelke​
George Noelke​
Intervenor​
Pro se Landowner
